CHAPTER II
THE EXISTING ENVIRONMENT
Climate
The climate of the Sarpy Creek area is of the continental type with relatively low humidity and characteristic extremes in temperature. Cold waves are common during the winter and are characterized by subzero temperatures, high winds, and blowing snow. During these cold waves, temperatures, may drop to below -50°F. The cold waves, however, seldom last longer than several days and are usually separated by periods of relatively mild, windy weather (Cordell, 1971). Summer temperatures typically exceed 100°F at some locations each year. However, hot spells, like cold waves, seldom last for extended periods and nighttime temperatures are rarely unpleasant in summer even when daytime temperatures are quite hot.
Meteorological data from three stations were utilized as the best estimate of long-term meteorological conditions at the Sarpy Creek site. These include the Billings airport (Logan Field), located 75 miles west of the Project Area; the Miles City Municipal Airport located 65 miles northeast of the Project Area; and the cooperative weather station at Colstrip, located 15 miles east-northeast of the Project Area. Evaporation data from Terry, located about 105 miles northeast of the Project area, have also been included. Recent short-term data from Colstrip was used to the maximum extent possible because of the proximity of Colstrip to the Project Area and the similarities between the two locations with regard to elevation, surrounding terrain, and general airshed characteristics.
